passages.quote: This remote indication is necessary for the monitoring of vital components located within inaccessible or remote areas.
An electrical synchro has two distinct advantages over mechanical indicators: (1) greater accuracy, and (2) simpler routing of remote indication.
The basic types are: transmitters, differential transmitters, receivers, differential receivers, and control transformers.
The transmitter, or synchro generator, consists of a rotor with a single winding and a stator with three windings placed 120 degrees apart.
The synchro receiver uses the voltage generated by each of the synchro generator windings to position the receiver rotor.
Hunting refers to the overshoot and undershoot that occur as the receiving device tries to match the sending device.
it incorporates a damping device to prevent hunting.
Control transformer synchros are used when only a voltage indication of angular position is desired.
The limit switch gives ON/OFF output that corresponds to valve position.
Limit switch failures are normally mechanical in nature.
In this case, local position indication should be used to verify equipment position.
Reed switches, illustrated in Figure 4, are more reliable than limit switches, due to their simplified construction.
As the magnet approaches the reed switch, the switch shuts. When the magnet moves away, the reed switch opens.
By using a large number of magnetic reed switches, incremental position can be measured.
If a reed switch is stuck shut, the open (closed) indication will be continuously illuminated.
The amount of current is proportional to the valve position.
An electrical short or open will cause the indication to fail at one extreme or the other.
If an increase or decrease in the potentiometer resistance occurs, erratic indicated valve position occurs.
Unlike the potentiometer position indicator, no physical connection to the extension is required.
A metal extension on the valve stem changes the coupling between the secondary coils.

passages.quote: Control functions are usually in the form of interlocks.
two valves may be interlocked to prevent both of the valves from being opened at the same time.
Control rod interlocks are normally used to prevent outward motion of certain rods unless certain conditions are met.
The accuracy and reliability of position indication instrumentation can be affected by ambient temperature and humidity.
Detection devices provide a method to determine the position of a valve or control rod.
The indicating and control circuitry provides for remote indication of valve or rod position and/or various control functions.

body.text: Position indicating instrumentation gives remote indication of control rod position and of the open or shut condition of important valves.
Synchros are self-synchronizing motors that electrically govern or follow the position of a mechanical indicator or device.

body.alt: Schematic symbols for synchro types, showing rotor and stator windings.

body.text: The rotor induces a voltage in each stator winding based on its angular position.

body.alt: Synchro transmitter wired to a synchro receiver.

checks.q: What are the two advantages of an electrical synchro over mechanical indicators?
o: Greater accuracy and simpler routing of remote indication
checks.x: An electrical synchro has greater accuracy and simpler routing of remote indication.

checks.q: What does the damping device in a synchro receiver prevent?
checks.x: The receiver incorporates a damping device to prevent hunting.

checks.q: How many stator windings does a synchro transmitter have?
checks.x: The stator has three windings placed 120 degrees apart.

body.text: A limit switch is a mechanical device. An extension on a valve shaft mechanically trips it as the valve moves.

body.alt: Valve stem with an extension between two limit switches for open and shut.

body.text: Normally limit switches provide full open or full shut indications. Many are the push-button variety, with spring pressure opening the switch.

body.alt: Reed switches beside a valve stem extension carrying a permanent magnet.

body.text: Reed switches are flexible ferrous strips placed near the travel of the extension, and the extension is a permanent magnet.
Failures are normally limited to a reed switch stuck open or stuck shut.
If a reed switch is stuck open, the indication for that switch stays extinguished regardless of position.

checks.q: What kind of failure is normal for limit switches?
checks.x: Limit switch failures are normally mechanical in nature.

checks.q: Why are reed switches more reliable than limit switches?
checks.x: Reed switches are more reliable than limit switches due to their simplified construction.

checks.q: A reed switch is stuck shut. What does the indication show?
checks.x: If a reed switch is stuck shut, the indication will be continuously illuminated.

body.text: A potentiometer indicator gives accurate position throughout the travel. The extension is physically attached to a variable resistor, so its movement changes the circuit's current.

body.alt: Valve stem connected to a variable resistor in a circuit with an indicator.
Valve with its extension shaft moving between the primary and secondary windings of a transformer.

body.text: The extension acts as the movable core of a transformer. Moving it varies the inductance and output voltage in proportion to position.

LVDT failures are limited to rare electrical faults. An open primary winding fails the indication to a value equal to zero differential voltage, normally mid-stroke. A failed secondary winding indicates full open or full closed.

checks.q: What does an electrical short or open do to a potentiometer valve position indicator?
o: Fails the indication at one extreme or the other
checks.x: An electrical short or open will cause the indication to fail at one extreme or the other.

checks.q: How does an LVDT differ from a potentiometer position indicator?
o: It needs a magnet on the extension
No physical connection to the extension is required
It only shows open or shut
checks.x: Unlike the potentiometer, no physical connection to the extension is required.

body.text: Reed and limit switches give open and closed indications and control functions. Potentiometer and LVDT indicators give accurate position throughout their travel.
A pump's isolation valves may be interlocked with it, to prevent starting with the valves shut or to stop the pump if a valve shuts.

checks.q: What does the indicating and control circuitry of a position indicator provide?
o: The electrical power to the valve
checks.x: It provides remote indication of valve or rod position and/or various control functions.

checks.q: What form do position control functions usually take?
checks.x: Control functions are usually in the form of interlocks.

checks.x: Accuracy and reliability can be affected by ambient temperature and humidity.

examples.title: Stuck open reed switch
examples.problem: A reed switch is stuck open. What does the operator see as the valve moves?
examples.answer: The indication stays extinguished regardless of valve position.

examples.title: Open LVDT primary
examples.problem: An LVDT primary winding opens. What does the indication do?
steps: The output falls to zero differential voltage
examples.answer: It fails to a predetermined value, normally mid-stroke.

facts.q: What is hunting in a synchro?
facts.a: The overshoot and undershoot that occur as the receiving device tries to match the sending device.

facts.q: How does a limit switch indicate position?
facts.a: An extension on a valve shaft trips it, giving an ON/OFF output that corresponds to valve position.

facts.q: How can reed switches show incremental position?
facts.a: By using a large number of magnetic reed switches along the travel.

facts.q: What happens if potentiometer resistance increases or decreases?
What do control rod interlocks do?
facts.a: They prevent outward motion of certain rods unless certain conditions are met.

summary.text: A basic synchro system has a transmitter and a receiver whose shaft follows the transmitter's electrical position.
Limit switches and reed switches give ON/OFF position indication.
Potentiometer and LVDT position indicators provide accurate indication of valve and rod position throughout their travel.
Ambient temperature and humidity can affect position indication instrumentation.
